issue: h₂ḱh₃ih₁tā́m is optative 3DU, but its subject ǵʰwḗr ('the beast') is singular; should be 3sg h₂ḱh₃yéh₁t. (Minor point: 'lie down' uses two different stems, légʰoh₂ vs légʰyoyh₁ent.)
h₂n̥rṓm is gen. pl. ('of men') but it is the subject of gʷémt ('A man came to him'); should be nom. sg. h₂nḗr, the form the text uses later.
h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe sléh₂gʷt 'and she took it': 'it' is the silver (neuter h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom), so the pronoun should be h₁íd; fem. h₁íh₂m̥ points back to the wool.
déh₂nu is addressed as 'River goddess' but every agreeing word is neuter (HéHḱu, ń̥dʰgʷʰitom, anaphoric h₁íd), so the PIE says 'River', not a personified (feminine, cf. Ved. Dā́nu) goddess.

A faithful respelling of Schleicher (1868) 'Avis akvāsas ka'. Pre-laryngeal notation (a-vocalism, akwāsas with a double Indo-Iranian-style ending, ka as a free word rather than enclitic -kʷe), so it is not well formed by modern standards; acceptable only if labelled as a historical scholarly version.

h₂ewseti is the lexeme 'draw water' (and it is written without an accent), used here for 'singes'; the right word is h₁éwseti (*h₁ews- 'burn', Lat. ūrō, Ved. óṣati). Minor: the plural imperatives bʰugté/dʰgʷʰh₂té/litté address two singular vocatives, where a dual would match the engine's dual agreement elsewhere.
tpḗrsneh₂h₁ 'two heels': nom./acc. dual of an eh₂-stem made with bare -h₁, the same as the instr. sg.; the handbook form is *-eh₂-ih₁ (Ved. -e, OCS -ě).

bʰérontu is 3pl imperative ('let them carry'), but the request is addressed to the boatman (voc. néh₂uwiHre), so it should be 2sg bʰére. Also sddʰí is 2sg though the boatman is speaking to the two men (2du/2pl expected), and the two men use 1pl déh₃womes with 2pl h₁opéyete instead of duals.
pl̥h₁éwih₂m̥ h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m means 'much wool', not 'more wool' (no comparative).
h₂usbʰós is dat./abl. pl. of h₂éwsōs, used as the subject of h₁ludʰét ('Then Dawn came'); should be nom. h₂éwsōs.

A faithful respelling of Schleicher (1868) 'Avis akvabhjams ā vavakat: kard aghnutai mai vidanti manum akvams agantam'. Pre-laryngeal and obsolete by modern standards (a-vocalism, -bʰyams, aghnutai, preverb ā); acceptable only if labelled as a historical scholarly version.
pr̥wé is aorist 1DU of *per- 'get through' ('we two crossed'), but the subject is 'he' (the trader); should be 3sg pért.
